Odd one out: Monday, Tuesday, March, Friday

q: Today is Monday. What day will it be in 10 days?
Today is Wednesday. What day was it 5 days ago?
Today is Sunday. What day will it be in 30 days?
The 1st of a month is a Monday. What day is the 15th?
e: The 15th is 14 days later = exactly 2 weeks → the same day, Monday.

q: Today is Tuesday. What day will it be in 100 days?
Today is Friday. What day was it 20 days ago?
e: 20 ÷ 7 leaves 6; count back 6 from Friday → Saturday.

q: Today is Saturday. What day will it be in 50 days?

Today is Monday. What day will it be in 365 days?
e: 365 ÷ 7 leaves 1; one year moves the weekday forward by one → Tuesday.

q: The 10th of a month is a Friday. What day is the 24th?
e: The 24th is 14 days later = exactly 2 weeks → the same day, Friday.

q: All fish can swim. A shark is a fish. So a shark?
No insects have bones. An ant is an insect. So an ant?
All squares have equal sides. This shape is NOT a square. So its sides?
e: A non-square can still have equal sides (a rhombus). Can't tell.

q: Some students walk to school. Maria is a student. So Maria?
e: 'Some' students ≠ all students — Maria may or may not.

q: Every key on the ring opens a door. This key is on the ring. So this key?
No cats are dogs. Rex is a dog. So Rex?
e: If no cats are dogs, no dog is a cat.

q: All roses have thorns. This flower has thorns. So this flower?
e: Thorns don't make it a rose — other flowers have thorns too.

q: Some books are long. All long things take time. So some books?
e: The long books take time — so some books do.

q: All whales are mammals. No mammals are fish. So whales?
e: Whales are mammals, and no mammal is a fish.

q: Some apples are green. Some green things are sour. So some apples are sour?
e: Two 'somes' don't connect — the green apples may not be the sour things.

q: All the guides are patient. Sam is not patient. So Sam?
e: If all guides are patient, an impatient person can't be one.

q: Most birds can fly. An ostrich is a bird. So an ostrich?
e: 'Most' is not 'all' — the ostrich might be an exception.

q: PARSIMONIOUS is to MONEY as TACITURN is to:
e: Both describe giving out very little of something. Parsimonious = sparing with money; taciturn = sparing with words.

q: COMPOSER is to SCORE as ARCHITECT is to:
e: Each makes the plan that others build from. The score is not the music and the blueprint is not the building — the building is the finished product, not the plan.

q: PLACATE is to ANGER as ALLEVIATE is to:
e: Both verbs mean 'to lessen the thing named'. Placate reduces anger; alleviate reduces pain.

q: DROUGHT is to WATER as FAMINE is to:
e: Each names a severe shortage. A drought is a shortage of water; a famine is a shortage of food.

q: MAVERICK is to CONFORM as HERMIT is to:
e: Define each by what it refuses. A maverick refuses to conform; a hermit refuses to socialize.

q: CYGNET is to SWAN as GOSLING is to:
e: Young animal to adult. A cygnet grows into a swan; a gosling grows into a goose.

q: Although the evidence was ___, the jury reached a verdict within an hour.
e: 'Although' signals a contrast, so the blank must make the fast verdict surprising. Thin evidence is surprising; overwhelming evidence would make speed expected.

q: Her explanation was so ___ that even the specialists asked her to repeat it.
e: If specialists needed it repeated, it was hard to follow. Abstruse means hard to understand; lucid means the opposite.

q: The senator's ___ answers frustrated reporters, who wanted a straight yes or no.
e: The contrast is with 'a straight yes or no', so the answers dodged. Equivocal means deliberately open to more than one reading.

q: Far from being ___, the new policy simply restated rules that had stood for decades.
e: 'Far from being X' followed by 'simply restated old rules' tells you it was not new. Novel means new.

q: The critic's praise was ___: he admired the acting while calling the plot absurd.
e: The colon explains the blank — praise with a limit attached. Qualified means limited by conditions.

q: ANTONYM of PROLIFERATE:
e: Proliferate = increase rapidly in number, so the opposite is to shrink away: dwindle. Multiply is a synonym planted as a trap.

q: ANTONYM of PROFLIGATE:
e: Profligate = recklessly extravagant with money. Its opposite is careful with money: thrifty. Wasteful is a synonym.

q: ANTONYM of EPHEMERAL:
e: Ephemeral = lasting a very short time. Enduring = lasting a long time. Fleeting means the same as ephemeral.

q: ANTONYM of GARRULOUS:
e: Garrulous = excessively talkative, so its opposite is unwilling to speak: reticent.

q: ANTONYM of EXACERBATE:
e: Exacerbate = make worse. Assuage = soothe or ease. Aggravate is another word for exacerbate.

q: SYNONYM of RECALCITRANT:
e: Recalcitrant = stubbornly resisting authority. Obstinate = stubborn. Compliant is the opposite.

q: SYNONYM of PERFUNCTORY:
e: Perfunctory = done as a routine, with the least effort that will pass. Cursory = hasty and superficial.

q: SYNONYM of INTRANSIGENT:
e: Intransigent = refusing to change position. Uncompromising says the same thing.

q: SYNONYM of LACONIC:
e: Laconic = using very few words. Terse means the same. Verbose is the opposite.

q: Which does NOT belong: Sonnet, Haiku, Limerick, Novella
e: The other three are fixed poetic forms defined by their line count. A novella is prose fiction.

q: Which does NOT belong: Bronze, Brass, Steel, Copper
e: Bronze, brass and steel are alloys — metals mixed with something else. Copper is a pure element.

q: Which does NOT belong: Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Mercury
e: The other three are giant planets made mostly of gas and ice. Mercury is small and rocky.

q: Which two entries are exactly identical?    A) RX-40921-BT    B) RX-40912-BT    C) RX-40921-BT    D) RX-4O921-BT
e: Compare one character at a time. B swaps 21 for 12. D uses the letter O where the others have a zero. A and C match exactly.

q: Which entry differs from the other three?    A) 550-XJ-8801    B) 550-XJ-8801    C) 55O-XJ-8801    D) 550-XJ-8801
e: Scan one field at a time rather than reading the whole string. In C the second character is the letter O, not a zero.

q: Next in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___
e: Write the gaps underneath: 4, 6, 8, 10. They rise by 2 each time, so the next gap is 12 — and 30 + 12 = 42.

q: Next in the series: 3, 7, 16, 35, 74, ___
e: Each step doubles and adds a counter that grows by one: ×2+1, ×2+2, ×2+3, ×2+4. Next is 74×2+5 = 153.

q: Next in the series: 64, 32, 48, 24, 36, ___
e: Two rules alternate: halve, then multiply by one and a half. 36 comes after a ×1.5, so this step halves: 18.

q: Next in the series: 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ___
e: The multiplier climbs: ×2, ×3, ×4, ×5. Next is ×6, so 120 × 6 = 720.

q: Next in the series: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ___
e: Each term is double the one before plus 1. 95 × 2 + 1 = 191.

q: A jacket costs $80. It is discounted 15%, then the sale price is raised 10%. Final price?
A number increased by 25% gives 90. What was the number?
e: 90 is 125% of the original, so divide: 90 ÷ 1.25 = 72. Check it — 10% of 72 is 7.2, so 25% is 18, and 72 + 18 = 90.

q: In a class of 40, 60% are girls. Six more boys join. What percent of the class is now girls?
e: 10% of 40 is 4, so 60% is 24 girls and 16 boys. Adding 6 boys gives 22 boys and 46 students. 24 ÷ 46 is just over half → 52%.

q: A share price falls 30%, then rises 30%. Compared with the start it is now:
e: Start at 100. Down 30% → 70. The rise acts on 70, not 100: 30% of 70 is 21, giving 91. That is 9% below the start.

q: Two numbers are in the ratio 3:5 and add to 96. The larger number is:
e: Think in shares: 3 + 5 = 8 equal shares. 96 ÷ 8 = 12 per share. The larger number holds 5 shares: 5 × 12 = 60.

q: A mix uses flour and sugar in the ratio 7:3. In 2 kg of the mix, how much sugar?
e: 7 + 3 = 10 shares. 2 kg ÷ 10 = 200 g per share. Sugar holds 3 shares: 3 × 200 = 600 g.

q: If 4 painters finish a room in 9 hours, how long would 6 painters take at the same rate?
e: Find the total work first: 4 × 9 = 36 painter-hours. Split it among 6 people: 36 ÷ 6 = 6 hours. More painters means less time, so the answer must be under 9.

q: The average of five numbers is 20. Four of them are 15, 18, 22 and 25. The fifth is:
e: Five numbers averaging 20 must total 100. The four given add to 80, so the missing one is 20.

q: A student averages 78 over four tests. What score on a fifth test lifts the average to 80?
e: Four tests at 78 total 312. Five tests at 80 need 400. The fifth test has to cover the gap: 400 − 312 = 88.

q: A train leaves at 2:45 pm and arrives at 6:20 pm. How long is the journey?
e: Go to the easy landmark first: 2:45 to 6:45 is exactly 4 hours. Arriving at 6:20 is 25 minutes earlier, so 4 h − 25 min = 3 h 35 min.

q: Pens cost $3 and notebooks $7. Someone buys 12 items for $64. How many notebooks?
e: If all 12 were pens the bill would be $36. Every swap from pen to notebook adds $4. You need $64 − $36 = $28 more, and 28 ÷ 4 = 7 notebooks.

q: A tank is 3/8 full. After adding 15 litres it is 3/4 full. What is its capacity?
e: Put both over 8: 3/4 is 6/8, so the water added is 6/8 − 3/8 = 3/8 of the tank. If 3/8 is 15 litres then 1/8 is 5 litres, and the full tank is 8 × 5 = 40 litres.

q: The turns alternate: 90° counter-clockwise, then 180°. What comes next?
e: Up turns 90° counter-clockwise to point left. Left turns 180° to point right. Right turns 90° counter-clockwise to point up.

q: The dot count grows by a widening step. How many dots come next?
e: Count each figure: 1, 3, 6. The jumps are 2 then 3, so the next jump is 4 — giving 6 + 4 = 10.

q: Which shape has a number of sides that is NOT a factor of 12?
e: Count the sides: 3, 4, 5, 6. Twelve divides evenly by 3, 4 and 6, but not by 5 — so the pentagon is the odd one out.

q: A regular polygon has interior angles of 150°. How many sides does it have?
e: At each corner the outside angle is 180 − 150 = 30°. The outside angles of any polygon always total 360°, so there are 360 ÷ 30 = 12 corners, and so 12 sides.

q: A shape is flipped in a vertical mirror, then turned 180°. The combined result is the same as:
o: A flip in a horizontal mirror
A flip in a vertical mirror
e: Track one corner. The vertical mirror swaps left and right; the 180° turn swaps left-right AND top-bottom. Left and right end up back where they started, so only top and bottom have swapped — that is a horizontal mirror.
